_comment: Seed-ready DigitizedDataset rows for PSPP_MATERIALS_PLAN.md pspp-7. Transcribed 2026-07-18 by Claude from Dustin's photographs of Davidovits, 'Geopolymer Chemistry and Applications', Chapter 5 (title confirmed by Dustin 2026-07-18; edition still to note) (running heads: 'Structure of poly(siloxonate) solutions, soluble alkali silicates' / 'Poly(siloxonate) and polysilicate, soluble silicate, Si:Al=1:0' — Davidovits-style terminology; exact edition citation TO CONFIRM with Dustin before the module repo goes public). Tables are exact transcriptions; figure reads are marked by digitization_method and error. Extrapolation policy is UNSUPPORTED everywhere per plan invariant I6.

datasets.name: na-silicate-solution-polymerization-vs-mr
datasets.source_reference: Geopolymer book Ch.5, Table 5.4, p.101 (after Engler 1974)

source_conditions.note: Equilibrium values; p.101 text: an equilibrium develops for any given solution composition; rapid rearrangement of polymer species occurs when the solution is diluted or extra alkali is added; equilibrium is reached more quickly for lower-MR solutions.

datasets.name: k-silicate-solution-polymerization-vs-mr
datasets.source_reference: Geopolymer book Ch.5, Table 5.5, p.101 (after Engler 1974)

source_conditions.note: Same Engler (1974) source and equilibrium caveats as Table 5.4.

validity_domain.note: Steep jump between MR 3.62 (n=5.3) and 3.97 (n=14.1) — linear interpolation in that last interval is questionable; interpolation there should carry a wide band.

datasets.name: na-siloxonate-glass-to-solution-q-depolymerization

source_conditions.system: Na-siloxonate: parent alkali glass vs the aqueous solution obtained by dissolving it
source_conditions.caveat_q4_artifact: Fig 5.12 caption (same page): in liquid-state 29Si NMR of sodium silicate + NaOH at MR=1.6, the Q4 specie is an equipment artifact. Solution Q4 values from liquid NMR must carry this provenance warning — note the nonzero Q4=7% for MR 3.28 solution below.
source_conditions.mechanism_context: Section 5.6.3: dissolution depolymerizes higher-Q glass species into lower-Q soluble Na-siloxonate molecules.
source_conditions.sum_anomaly: AS PRINTED, two solution rows do not sum to 100%: MR 1.0 solution = 92, MR 2.0 solution = 110 (photo re-checked 2026-07-18, digits confirmed). All glass rows sum to exactly 100. Either the book rounds/omits minor species or the book has a typo — verify against another copy before normalizing; never silently rescale.

datasets.interpolation_policy: none — fixed reference mappings at the listed MRs only (no general kinetic law in source)

validity_domain.note: Discrete rows only; do NOT interpolate between MRs without marking the output estimated.

datasets.name: silicate-solution-viscosity-vs-temperature

source_conditions.concentration: SAME concentration for both series, but the value is NOT stated on the photographed page — treat as relative/reference curves, not absolute predictions for arbitrary solutions
source_conditions.page_text: p.110: at the same MR, viscosity of potassium silicate solutions is 10x lower than sodium silicate solutions.

datasets.digitization_method: printed point-value labels read from photograph (each marker carries its numeric label in the figure) — NOT a curve trace
datasets.digitization_error: labels exact; temperature positions read from axis gridlines, est. +/-1 degC

datasets.name: na-siloxonate-solubility-vs-temperature
datasets.status: PROVISIONAL-LOW-CONFIDENCE — needs re-digitization from a straight-on photo or scan before any engine consumes it
datasets.digitization_method: coarse visual curve read from an angled photograph — shape and axis ranges reliable, individual point values NOT
datasets.digitization_error: est. +/-50 g/L and +/-5 degC; RE-SHOOT REQUESTED
datasets.qualitative_shape: All three series increase with temperature over 10-90 degC within the 300-900 g/L axis range. The MR=1 (metasilicate pentahydrate) and MR=2 (disilicate) curves lie substantially above the MR=3.3 (trisilicate) curve and cross each other in the mid-temperature region; MR=3.3 stays lowest throughout. Numeric points intentionally omitted pending re-digitization.

qualitative_claims.claim: Solution polymer-species equilibrium rearranges rapidly on dilution or extra alkali addition; equilibrium is reached more quickly for lower-MR solutions.
qualitative_claims.use: provenance caveat on any engine treating Tables 5.4/5.5 values as fixed for a modified solution

qualitative_claims.claim: Liquid-state 29Si NMR Q4 peak at MR=1.6 (Na silicate + NaOH) is an equipment artifact.
qualitative_claims.use: EvidenceMethod warning attached to solution Q4 values from liquid NMR

qualitative_claims.claim: Commercial alkali-silicate solutions have pH 10.9-13.5; MR=1 Na-metasilicates exhibit pH above 13.5 and are corrosive in solutions above 5% content; alkali silicate solutions have very high buffer capacity (sharp pH change only after neutralization of the alkali); pH is the most important characteristic determining stability of high-modulus silicate solutions (inclination to gel or coagulation); stability increases steadily as pH increases.
qualitative_claims.use: activator-solution admissibility constraints + safety notes for mixing-process definitions

qualitative_claims.claim: pH of an alkali silicate solution depends on MR and above all on M2O concentration (Figure 5.21, not yet photographed).
qualitative_claims.use: marks Fig 5.21 as a future digitization target

qualitative_claims.claim: Na-metasilicate (MR=1) exists in four forms: anhydrous Na2O.SiO2 (manufactured at 900 degC in the furnace) and hydrous pentahydrate (5H2O), hexahydrate (6H2O), nonahydrate (9H2O); hydrous forms produced hydrothermally or by blending higher-MR solutions with NaOH; concentrated Na-metasilicate solutions are inherently unstable and liable to crystallize, hence metasilicates are supplied in dry form (rotary-bed crystallization or belt technique).
qualitative_claims.use: commercial-precursor presets for CompositionNormalizer (pspp-6): hydrate identity fixes the oxide+water composition exactly

qualitative_claims.claim: Powdered hydrous alkali silicate powders are produced by spray-drying poly(siloxonate) solutions of the desired MR.
qualitative_claims.use: precursor-form vocabulary (solid silicate powder as activator form)

qualitative_claims.claim: MR = 1.032 x WR for sodium silicate; MR = 1.568 x WR for potassium silicate; practical MR range for sodium silicates in praxis is 0.4-4.0.
qualitative_claims.use: encoded + selftest-pinned in pspp.composition_math (mr_from_wr, PRACTICAL_MR_RANGE_NA)

qualitative_claims.claim: Table 5.1 commercial silicate MRs: sodium orthosilicate Na4SiO4 = 0.5, sodium metasilicate Na2SiO3 = 1.0, sodium disilicate Na2Si2O5 = 2.0, sodium polysilicate Na2O.3.3SiO2 = 3.30.
qualitative_claims.use: COMMERCIAL_SILICATE_MR presets in pspp.composition_math

qualitative_claims.claim: Manufacture routes (Fig 5.1, after Crosfield 1997): furnace route (sand + soda ash -> alkali glass -> milling/agglomeration -> dissolving -> blending -> waterglass solutions -> spray drying/compaction -> powdered/granular silicates) and hydrothermal route (sand + caustic soda -> silicate liquor -> rotary crystallisation -> pentahydrate; belt crystallisation -> nonahydrate). Silica glass converts to poly(siloxonate) by stepwise Si-O-Si cleavage: bridging oxygens -> non-bridging Si-ONa (Section 5.3.1).
qualitative_claims.use: process-vocabulary evidence for pspp-4 MaterialProcessDefinition rows (real manufacture graph example)

qualitative_claims.claim: Q-species distribution curves for Na-silicate glasses (Fig 5.4) and K-silicate glasses (Fig 5.5) vs MR, adapted from Maekawa et al. (1991); anchor text: MR=1 metasilicate -> almost completely Q2 (small Q1+Q3); MR=2 disilicate -> virtually only Q3 (small Q2+Q4); MR=4 tetrasilicate -> Q3 and Q4 at 50% each. Na curves cross-confirm Table 5.6 glass rows exactly.
qualitative_claims.use: digitized into modules/pspp datasets_seed (na/k-glass-q-distribution-vs-mr) — Tier 2 UNBLOCKED, q_glass_distribution engine live

qualitative_claims.claim: Industrial silicate glasses are phase MIXTURES at eutectic-anchored compositions: neutral Na-glass 76.5 wt% SiO2 (beta-IV disilicate + VII quartz), alkaline Na-glass 66 wt% SiO2 (III metasilicate + beta-IV disilicate), K-glass 71 wt% SiO2 (phase III tetrasilicate). Eutectic points: 66% and 76% SiO2 (Na), 71% SiO2 (K). Fabrication-parameter changes strongly affect nominal composition and geopolymeric properties. Fig 5.3 = K2O.SiO2 phase diagram (Kracek et al. 1937), phases I K2SiO3 / II K2O.2SiO2 / III K2O.4SiO2 / IV tridymite / V quartz / VI cristobalite.
qualitative_claims.use: industrial-glass composition presets; Fig 5.3 liquidus curves = future digitization target only if phase modeling needs them

qualitative_claims.claim: Hydrothermal route: direct dissolution of sand/siliceous products in caustic NaOH/KOH inside autoclaves (aggressive conditions); industrially restricted to hydrated metasilicate MR=1. Silica-fume dissolution in alkaline solution is a lab-scale alternative route; adding NaOH to lower the modulus of a high-modulus solution at the customer's site is NOT generally recommended — adjust during blending at the chemical plant.
qualitative_claims.use: pspp-4 process definitions: route constraints + admissibility notes for activator preparation

qualitative_claims.claim: MAS-NMR: alkali silicate glass composition is not entirely random. Molecular structure: triple-helix poly(siloxonate)/poly(siloxo) SiO2 chains; alkaline attack starts at the weaker inter-helix siloxane bonds, leaving individual helices intact to a degree; alkalination forms Si-ONa terminal units (NBO) at the surface.
qualitative_claims.use: mechanistic context for dissolution reaction rules (competing-hypothesis register, never hardcoded)

qualitative_claims.claim: Fig 8.21 two-phase transport selection: Phase 1 outer faces/edges reaction with Na+/K+/OH- AND Q0-Q3 siloxonates -> albite pathway (Si:Al=3); Phase 2 inner particulate reaction with ONLY Na+/K+/OH- (interlayers swell; even Q0 too big to penetrate) -> nepheline pathway (Si:Al=1). Rüscher 2010 molybdate: polymeric silicate chains condense first from waterglass, then slow alumino-silicate 3D network surrounds them.
qualitative_claims.use: encoded as site-constrained ReactionRule rows (surface-only vs interior-only) in pspp.reaction_network

qualitative_claims.claim: Phillipsite route (§8.5.3, pp.188-189): ideal Na-PSS structure NaAlSi2O6 (Si:Al=2) via monomeric ortho-siloxonate Q0; Q0 obtained by mild depolymerization of Q1/Q2 ONLY when the Na-silicate solution has MR < 1.20; two alternative condensation paths 6a (Q0+ortho-sialate -> linear -> branched quadratic) and 6b (2 ortho-sialates -> quadratic di-sialate + 2 Q0 -> same branched quadratic); phillipsite is zeolitic (micro-porosity, higher zeolitic water).
qualitative_claims.use: encoded as ReactionRule rows; MR<1.20 threshold noted pending a threshold-shaped ReactionWindow variant

qualitative_claims.claim: US Patent 4,349,386 / FR 79.22041 Table A reactant-mixture ranges for (Na,K)-PSS: (Na2O,K2O)/SiO2 0.20-0.28, SiO2/Al2O3 3.5-4.5 (deliberately above stoichiometric 2), H2O/(Na2O,K2O) 15-17.5, (Na2O,K2O)/Al2O3 0.8-1.20. US Patent 4,472,199 Table C for kaliophilite-related K-PS: K2O/SiO2 0.25-0.48, SiO2/Al2O3 3.3-4.5, H2O/Al2O3 10-25. K-PS formula K2O:2SiO2:Al2O3:H2O; anhydrous feldspathoid Kn(-Si-O-Al-O-)n.wH2O, w in [0,1]. TGA discriminator: K-PS <=5% water loss to 325C (thermal-shock resistant, hard 5 Mohs, brittle) vs (Na,K)-PSS 21-29% loss 100-500C (zeolitic water; dehydroxylate <=400C before high-T use). A 'preferably...' clause on p.191 was cut off in the photo — re-shoot if finer grading wanted.
qualitative_claims.use: SEEDED as 7 ReactionWindow rows (binary-range semantics); TGA discriminator on framework-kaliophilite species notes

qualitative_claims.claim: p.193 GRADED window detail (US 4,472,199 excerpt): preferably K2O/Al2O3 ~1.3-1.52 and SiO2/Al2O3 ~4.0-4.2; higher ratios induce a free potassium-silicate phase + K-silicate migration disturbing physical/mechanical properties; K2O/Al2O3 < 1.1 and SiO2/Al2O3 < 3.7 -> numerous cracks, unusable for molded objects. Table C 4th row: K2O/Al2O3 0.9-1.60.
qualitative_claims.use: recorded on the k-ps ReactionWindow rows; asymmetric ideal/acceptable/failure bands await a threshold-shaped window variant

qualitative_claims.claim: K analogues prove rule generality (pp.194-196): steps 1-5 identical to Na (with K+); kalsilite via condensation of THREE ortho-sialates -> hexagonal cyclo-tri-sialate (KOH regenerated); leucite via Q0 + two ortho-sialates -> cyclo-di-sialate-siloxo, Q0 again requiring mild Q1/Q2 depolymerization at MR<1.20 (same threshold as Na). Kriven leucite-ceramic route: crush K2O.Al2O3.4SiO2.7.5H2O geopolymer, die-press, sinter 1200C/12h (~3um leucite grains in remnant amorphous geopolymer matrix), anneal 1400C/5h. Crystallization studies: Barbosa/MacKenzie 2003 (leucite+kalsilite signs at 1000C, melting to 1400C), Trautman 2005 (-> kalsilite), Duxson 2005a (kaliophilite/kalsilite + leucite above 700C).
qualitative_claims.use: encoded as K-route ReactionRule rows; Kriven route = future MaterialProcessDefinition chain example

qualitative_claims.claim: Steps 1-5 mechanism detail (pp.181-182): Step 1 alkalination forms tetravalent-Al side group O3-Si-O-Al-(OH)3(-)Na+ (Al(V) alumoxyl -Al=O route §8.3.1, or Al-O-Al cleavage + hydroxylation §8.3.2); steps 2-4 cleave the poly(siloxo) layer, isolating the ortho-sialate; step 5 reacts basic siloxo Si-O(-) with Na+/K+ -> Si-ONa/Si-OK terminals. Na vs K kinetics differ slightly (K+ larger); MK-750 poly(siloxo) backbone remains practically intact.
qualitative_claims.use: ortho-sialate-formation rule upgraded to book-supported with this topology detail

qualitative_claims.claim: Al-coordination reaction roles (pp.176-178): Al(V) reacts first (rapid exotherm 1, 1h hardening); Al(IV) slower kinetics (2h peak; major in fly-ash systems); Al(VI) needs most energy/time (4-4.5h peak, highest strength). Chamotte (kaolinitic clays calcined 1050-1100C): high Al(IV), NO Al(V) -> very slow reaction, exotherm undetectable. Metakaolin calcination temperature (1000-1100C) converts Al(V) toward Al(IV)=Al(VI) and slows geopolymerization. Setting-vs-MR classes and cure-temperature exotherm ladder encoded as datasets.
qualitative_claims.use: Al-speciation descriptors for pspp-3 structure rows + process admissibility notes

benchmark_cases.name: mk750-na-pss-mr182

inputs.as_printed_discrepancy: formula implies H2O/Na2O = 15.45 but the ratio list prints 17.20 — both kept, never reconciled silently

observed_outcomes.phases_after_750C: nepheline (NaAlSiO4, Si:Al=1) + albite (NaAlSi3O8, Si:Al=3) coexisting ~50/50; bulk = NaAlSi2O6 (Si:Al=2); solid solution at nano scale; XRD-crystalline only after heat treatment >500C
observed_outcomes.duxson_2005a: above 500C nepheline forms with Na plus a not-well-defined component instead of albite
observed_outcomes.favier_2013_two_step: step 1 (<15 min): Si:Al 2-3 aluminosilicates at grain boundaries, solution still Q0-Q3 oligomers; step 2: hardening, second modulus rise, Si:Al=1 chemistry with only NaOH, no siloxonates
observed_outcomes.mr_speciation: MR=1.0 generates more Q0 and less Q2-Q3 than MR=1.82 (p.190)

benchmark_cases.use: the first PSPP benchmark validation case: composition_math reproduces the ratios (selftest-pinned); grade_composition places it inside ALL four Table A patent windows (selftest-pinned); framework branching per pp.184-189 mechanism rules

benchmark_cases.name: mk750-na-silicate-mr170-curing-series

inputs.recipe: Na-silicate MR SiO2:Na2O=1.70 100g + MK-750 63.47g (Na:Al=1), NO mineral fillers
inputs.procedure: planetary blender 300 RPM 10 min at 20C; cast small cylinders; oven 80C 15-20 min after mixing start; covered during setting; strength measured immediately after hot demolding, no drying
inputs.reactivity_reference: commercial MK-750 (Metamax) + Na-silicate: exotherm peak at 35 min, hardening complete at 60 min

observed_outcomes.strength_series: encoded as dataset mk750-strength-ph-vs-curing-time (2.83@1h Al(V), 5.66@2h Al(IV), 6.80/6.83@4-4.5h Al(VI), dip 4.26@8h, plateau 6.90@20h)
observed_outcomes.ph_mirror: pH anticorrelates with strength (12.38/12.51/12.44/12.22); dip = alkaline depolymerization then re-polymerization; free water sustains the equilibrium — drying stops it
observed_outcomes.al_speciation_bele\u00f1a: room-T: 10 min -> AlQ1(1Si)+AlQ2(2Si)+AlQ3(3Si); 90 min -> Q1/Q2 diminish; 4h -> all AlQ3(3Si); 1 day -> AlQ4(4Si) reticulation (steps 4-5 = AlQ1; steps 6-7 = AlQ2/AlQ3)

benchmark_cases.use: ReactionProgressModel v1 measured-curve calibration + performance-scenario validation

benchmark_cases.name: mk750-k-silicate-kalsilite-mixture

inputs.recipe: MK-750 + K-silicate solution MR=1.80; mixture = solid solution of K-PS (kaliophilite/kalsilite type) + potassium polysilicate; low-molecular K-polysilicate neutralized with 4.9% Ca(OH)2 (Dan Perera & Trautman 2005/2006)

observed_outcomes.windows: sits inside ALL Table C claimed ranges AND inside the p.193 preferred bands (SiO2/Al2O3 4.0-4.2, K2O/Al2O3 1.3-1.52)

benchmark_cases.use: K-family window validation + thermal phase-evolution benchmark
